In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Nb2SC has better structural, elastic, electronic and optical properties than the heavier Nb2SnC.
Nb2SC has a better dielectric property than Nb2SnC, and also that the former is a better superconducting material than the latter.
Nb2SC has a better performance in all the properties studied here, and is a better dielectic material, and also a better coating material than Nb2SnC.

the present work is the first ab-initio investigation on Nb2SC and the first detailed study of the optical properties of Nb2AC ( A=S, Sn) compounds.
, the present study of Nb2AC (AC = S and Sn) nanolaminates, provides a good insight into the structural, electronic, thermophysical and optical properties of these materials.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Nb2SnC phase, with its high superconducting transition temperature and better optical properties, may have a wide range of applications.
Nb2SC, Nb2SnC nanolaminates can be considered as promising materials for superconductivity, dielectric and coating applications.
the MAX phases Nb2SC andNb2SnC can be used as good electrical and optical materials, and also as moderately coupled superconducting materials.
